scope: R1 targeted revision only: B1 unified atomic lifecycle updates, B2 authenticated identity snapshot handover, B3 out-of-lock session teardown, B4 handshake-slot release, E1 order-independent structured case extraction, E2 fleet verifier correlation. No benchmark, M5 not started.

B1.problem: CompareAndReplace compared only generation and the two key ids, so an interleaved revoke/retire/policy edit was invisible; Revoke/Retire were lookup-then-unconditional-Replace and could write a whole stale Peer back
B1.fix: CompareAndReplace now compares peer revision and lifecycle unconditionally inside the write lock; Revoke/Retire go through setLifecycle -> CompareAndReplaceSnapshot, which asserts the whole snapshot and changes ONLY the lifecycle field; Rotation carries PreparedRevision/PreparedLifecycle from the real preparation read
interleavings_proven: stale revoke cannot wipe a newer rotation
stale retire cannot wipe a newer rotation
rotation detects an interleaved policy revision (revision-only change)
B1.disk_read_back: TestRegistryFailureLeavesOldGenerationUsable now re-opens the trust file and asserts generation N on disk
B1.fixture_adaptation: the review interposer hooked Replace; Revoke/Retire now commit through CompareAndReplaceSnapshot, so the hook was moved to that method and it POSITIVELY asserts that the interleaved rotation committed

B2.problem: serve re-looked-up the peer after the handshake and stamped the CURRENT key ids/generation onto a session that had authenticated with the OLD ones
B2.fix: Channel.PeerSnapshot() carries the immutable identity material actually verified (peer id, sign/agreement key ids, generation, registry revision); serve is split into handshakeConn / admitSession / business; admitSession reloads the registry, checks lifecycle, and compares the snapshot with the current entry; SessionState stores the authenticated values
B2.test: TestStaleGenerationSessionIsNotRegistered drives a real Suite 2 handshake on real TCP, commits a rotation, then admits the SAME channel: refused, never registered, and a fresh handshake on N+1 succeeds; TestAdmissionSucceedsWithoutInterleaving is the no-rotation control

B3.problem: Register registered defer Unlock before the teardown defer, so LIFO ran the teardown INSIDE the lock
B3.fix: lock covers only the map swap and counters; the superseded session is cancelled and closed after an explicit unlock
B3.tests: TestReviewReplacementCleanupRunsOutsideRegistryLock (TryLock proof), TestReviewSlowCloseDoesNotBlockOtherIdentities (channel-synchronised slow Close, no sleeps), plus the capacity/supersede regressions

B4.problem: the handshake slot was released only when the whole serve ended, so an established business session held a handshake slot
B4.fix: the slot is released by handshakeConn immediately after handshake.Server returns; one release point covers success, failure and cancellation; no limit was raised
B4.tests: TestHandshakeSlotReleasedBeforeBusiness (MaxHandshakes=1, first device holds a business session, second still handshakes), TestHandshakeSlotReleasedOnFailure (half-handshake takes the slot, then releases it; a real device can then use it)

E1.problem: the M4CASE parser matched a fixed field order, so adding record_replay_accepted silently dropped 3 of 13 replay cases from the evidence file while the run still reported PASS
E1.fix: order-independent marker + key=value scanner; unknown extra fields preserved; missing/empty required fields and bad tri-state values are recorded as problems and make the evidence run incomplete (non-zero exit); counts come from the data
E1.result: 13 cases extracted from the previous full stream (was 10); this run yields 14 because a new stale_generation case was added

E2.problem: the fleet verifier accepted evidence with a removed operation_id, business events pointing at a session that was never established, and a missing or duplicated bad-device row
E2.fix: correlation by (run_id, peer_id, session_id) against established sessions; required operation_id / sample_id; ack-to-control matching by (run_id, device_id, session_id, operation_id); exactly one bad-device row with boolean ok=false and a real failure message; controls_sent counted from control-sent events
E2.real_data: the untouched 20x3 evidence still verifies PASS with 60 unique session ids

self_introduced_regressions_found_and_fi: the split serve emitted the handshake-established event twice (strict verifier: found 2)
the gateway terminal peer-closed outcome was marked incomplete, failing the no-incomplete check
the first slow-Close test asserted a count before the teardown provably reached Close
verification_gaps: the race detector still cannot run on this machine; the concurrency and interleave tests are functional, NOT race-detector results
SM2 key agreement still has no independent implementation cross-check
not_claimed: cross-process concurrent registry update safety (single-writer by policy only)
a security audit or compliance certification
may_proceed_note: M4.2-R1 closes the audit blockers B1-B4/E1-E2. The two verification gaps must be closed before deployment or any claim of complete verification. M5 metric definitions may be prepared; sampling stays closed.
